    Katarzyna Wreczycka

    AI/ML Scientist. Computational Biology. Multi-Omics.

    • Zurich, Switzerland
    • GitHub
    • Google Scholar
    • LinkedIn

    Zurich-based data scientist with 9+ years of experience in machine learning, biomedical research and software development. Here, I share insights from my academic and industry projects in data analysis disease (epi)genomics and tool development. This is my personal website.

    I trained in computer science and bioinformatics at the University of Warsaw’s Faculty of Mathematics, Informatics and Mechanics (MIMUW). I completed my Ph.D. as a doctoral researcher in Prof. Altuna Akalin’s group at the Bioinformatics and Omics Data Science Platform at MDC-BIMSB, where I co-developed computational methods, the BioCgenomation package, and the PiGx BS-seq workflow for disease epigenomics. This included integrating multiple NGS datasets to investigate technical biases in ChIP-seq. My research also examined epigenomic changes in neuroblastoma and cardiovascular disease using solid tissue and liquid-biopsy samples from blood and urine. At ETH Zurich (Laboratory of Nutrition and Metabolic Epigenetics, Laboratory of Regenerative and Muscle Biology) and the Functional Genomics Center Zurich I further explored scRNA-seq analysis, including germline chimerism.

    In industry and freelance collaborations, I have applied machine learning and deep learning to translational challenges, including prioritizing therapeutic targets for clinical trials, developing single-cell RNA-seq methods for endometriosis prediction, monitoring wastewater for chemical anomalies, and identifying blood-based biomarkers for cancer and autoimmune diseases.

    Research interests

    Rapid advances in molecular profiling create new opportunities to study disease through genomics, epigenomics, bulk and single-cell transcriptomics, spatial transcriptomics, imaging, and proteomics. I integrate these data using machine learning and deep learning to address biological and clinical questions, including developing liquid-biopsy approaches for minimally invasive disease monitoring. I am committed to advancing machine learning research in biomedicine to improve clinical decision-making.

    I’m open for collaborations. Feel free to contact me: katwre (at) gmail.com.
